scope: One bounded 1032-hour eight-aircraft risk-failure slice: 21 spaced requests per wave at two bases, fixed 128 seeded replications, System TOTAL-only per-replication results, and measured mission success, flight hours and failure counts.

parameters.profile_requests: 21 two-wave BASE-01 and 21 BASE-02 requests at 48-hour spacing

metric_contract.confidence: nominal two-sided 95% Student t interval over 128 per-replication results
metric_contract.interval_method: compute sample SD and standard error directly from the 128 Replications/System TOTAL rows; do not treat native ResultSummary RSM* fields as the sample standard errors
metric_contract.stock_backorder_and_resource_wait: descriptive aggregate only; no per-replication interval
metric_contract.seed_repeat: same input and seed checks execution repeatability, not another independent sample

acceptance_hypotheses: Two fresh, guarded session-0 SSH runs pass exact populated-table import/export, zero converter errors, only warning #108, source fingerprints and raw SHA closures while preserving GUI PID13340.
A report-only OUTRP export for each result exposes 128 unique Replications rows and two-unit System TOTAL rows with 128 unique IDs per unit. No per-replication TIME/SNAPS rows are requested.

First-rep events, aggregate report and per-replication fields reconcile for mission success fraction, aircraft flight hours and observed failure counts; source-bound fault and physical repair/supply path remain observable.
Each nominal 95% interval meets its predeclared metric-specific half-width target; any failure is reported as imprecise rather than accepted stability.
Native event logs and reports from the same-input repeat runs are byte-identical, with a separately documented difference for run-path-bearing CLI logs and invocation metadata.
Independent read-only replay verifies the local raw closure, input delta, report arithmetic and bounded interpretation before publication.
limitations: One installed SIMLOX CLI engine and one model family; no GUI calculation or cross-engine equivalence claim.
Confidence intervals summarize the configured pseudo-random replication stream; no population or independence proof.
Only the first replication is visible in ENLOG; later event timelines are not independently enumerated.
Supply, stock and resource observations are aggregate descriptions, not per-replication precision claims.
The native default report may contain a trailing comma; preserve the raw bytes and use a narrowly defined parser correction for analysis. The separate replication report must parse as strict JSON.
